Subject: Re: Recap & next steps - demo today (latency vs cost)

Elena - attaching a concise cost sketch and notes below. High level first, then assumptions.  

Quick numbers (approximate, illustrative) - assume 250K calls/day * 30d = 7.5M calls/month at 210 tokens/call => ~1.575B tokens/month.

- Hosted - standard (streaming on, smaller model family):
  - Unit cost: ~$0.80–$1.20 per 1M tokens (depending on chosen model).
  - Monthly: $1.26k – $1.89k per 1.5B tokens (this looks too low; see note below) - WAIT, corrected math below.

- Hosted - premium (low-latency profile, higher-cost model or dedicated slices):
  - Unit cost: ~$3–$6 per 1M tokens.
  - Monthly: $4.7k – $9.45k per 1.5B tokens.

- Dedicated (reserved capacity, SLO-backed P95 <250ms):
  - Typically a committed monthly seat - starting ~$15k/month for a small reserved pool; unit cost effectively ~$2–$4 per 1M tokens depending on utilization and burst patterns.

Important notes on the math: my initial quick calc had a mislabeled decimal - I fixed the examples in the attached pricing-deck. The main takeaway: at 1.5B tokens/month, you want to target an effective unit cost between $3–$6 per 1M tokens to keep within the $8k–$12k monthly allocation for the real-time flow (that maps to ~$4.7k–$9k). If your target is lower ($1–$2 /1M), we'd need a much higher model compression/quantization profile or significant batching which harms P95.

Latency vs cost trade-offs (summary):
- Streaming (token-by-token streaming to client) gives best perceived latency for end users - P95 dominated by network and first-token generation; more expensive because you can't batch well.
- Continuous batching (server-side) reduces $/token (better throughput) but increases P95 tail and is sensitive to qps distribution - can be tuned with max wait windows and dynamic batching.
- Dedicated reserved capacity gives predictable latency but requires committed spend; good when you need an SLA-backed P95 and know min traffic.

Concrete recommendation for FintechAI initial phase:
- Target: P95 <250ms. Start Hosted-premium trial for 4 weeks to validate latency with real traffic (use streaming for Web flows).
- If P95 is stable but costs are >$6/1M, evaluate Dedicated reserved slices (we can model a 6–12 month commit for lower unit economics).
- Use caching + prefix KV for repeated prompts to shave tokens and costs.

I've attached a corrected pricing sheet and a sample usage CSV so you can plug in your real traffic pattern.

Attachments: redwood-pricing-deck.pdf, usage-samples.csv

Happy to walk through numbers on a quick call - propose Fri Mar 27 10am PT?

Best,
Marissa

Subject: Re: Cost sketch + latency trade-offs - unit economics detail

Hi Elena - Rishi here (pricing & partnerships). Adding a few concrete unit-econ lines to make decisions easier. These are rough but conservative.

Assumptions
- 1.575B tokens/month (as Marissa calculated).
- Baseline hosted-standard model (quantized): throughput good but P95 ~350–450ms under your peak pattern if we rely on batching.
- Hosted-premium (low-latency profile / better kernels): P95 ~180–260ms with streaming; cost higher.

Unit economics (approx)
- Hosted-standard (batch optimized): $1.50 per 1M tokens -> Monthly ~= $2.36k. (May fail P95 target without tuning).
- Hosted-premium (streaming, low-latency): $4.50 per 1M tokens -> Monthly ~= $7.09k.
- Dedicated reserved slice (small pool, committed): effective $3.25 per 1M tokens -> Monthly ~= $5.12k + $12k commit baseline (this is illustrative; final depends on utilization).

Notes on batching vs streaming impact
- Batching can reduce raw $/token by 30–60% depending on request shape and model, but tail latency may increase 2–5x relative to streaming for low-latency flows.
- We support hybrid configs: streaming for Web front-end (first-token low latency) and batched backend scoring for heavy batch jobs.

If the commercial target is $8k–$12k/month for the real-time flow, Hosted-premium looks like the clean first step (fits budget at ~$7.1k) while giving room to tune. If you want sub-$4k, we need either: higher batching (accept latency), model quantization beyond current profiles, or a multi-month commit.

I'll prep a short pricing appendix you can share with procurement (Tom) - including sample contract language for a 20% commit discount.

-Rishi
